incident-bot: 🚨 Detect: sudden spike in paging + sustained KV cache growth in prod eu-west-1 at 2026-03-14T03:07Z. Alert: cache_size +5x, page-in rate up, scheduler fairness drop. Creating incident thread.
eli (oncall): seeing it, short requests tail latency climbing. dashboards: https://dash.redwood/internal/kv-cache?range=1h
meera (runtime): looks like continuous-batching window expanded for some workloads — long chats holding KV slots. Short single-turn requests are getting starved and hit paging.
sasha (infra): metrics: kv_cache.items: 20M -> 118M in 12m, page_ins/sec 30 -> 420, host swap alerts on worker pool a6.
chris (sre): impact estimate? any customer-facing errors or just latency?
remy (prod-eng): initial ping from support — 3 customers reported tokenization timeouts, a few 502s on hosted chat endpoints. Most 502s correlate with paging spikes.
eli (oncall): marking Severity: S2 for now — high tail latency, partial errors. Paging causing CPU thrash on some nodes.
meera (runtime): root hypothesis: a regression in the continuous batching rewriter (rollout env=prod ~ 02:55Z) increased max-prefix-grouping to 4x, combined with prefetch enabled -> huge KV retention per connection. Scheduler then groups long requests into oversized batches.
sasha (infra): confirmed a canary -> prod rollout at 02:53Z. Rollout id: rollout-prod-20260314-0253, commit abc1234.
chris (sre): immediate mitigations we can do: 1) toggle continuous-batching to conservative window 2) lower per-connection KV retention cap 3) enable short-request priority slotting 4) add emergency routing to fallback model variant.
meera (runtime): agree. I'll prepare a hotfix patch to revert the grouping param and add fairness guard. assembling diff now.
remy (prod-eng): I'll notify affected customers and open a ticket. ETA on hotfix?
meera (runtime): patch ready, tests pass in staging. hotpatch: runtime/continuous_batching: revert grouping multiplier and cap retention. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4221 (patch 4221).
eli (oncall): roll plan? advise conservative approach: first flip config flag to reduce risk, then deploy hotpatch if needed.
sasha (infra): I can toggle config remotely. Command: 
```
infractl set-config --env prod --key continuous_batch.window_ms --value 10 --scope runtime
infractl set-config --env prod --key kv_cache.max_entries_per_conn --value 2000 --scope runtime
```
Applying continuous_batch.window_ms drop from 50->10ms should reduce grouping.
ops-bot: 🟡 Running infractl change: request accepted, job id if-987654. Estimated apply ~ 30s per region.
(30s later)
ops-bot: ✅ infractl job if-987654 completed for eu-west-1.
meera (runtime): patching fairness guard now: one-liner to enable "batch_scheduler.fair_slotting=true" to prioritize low-token requests. Command: 
```
rbctl set batch_scheduler.fair_slotting=true --env prod --region eu-west-1
```
Applying...
sasha (infra): rolled fair_slotting true.
meera (runtime): restarting a subset of runtime workers gracefully to pick up config. Doing staggered 10% waves.
chris (sre): monitoring: page_in/sec dropping from 420 -> 90 over last 6m, kv_cache.items 118M -> 55M. Tail P99 latency for short requests dropped 2.6s -> 520ms. Good sign.
remy (prod-eng): support: sent initial customer note to 5 impacted accounts, offering post-incident review.
eli (oncall): do we still need the hotpatch PR?
meera (runtime): yes still roll PR to be safe — the config flip is mitigation, hotpatch will remove regression and add automated caps to prevent recurrence. I'll start canary deployment to 10% nodes.
ops-bot: Deploy canary runtime-patch-4221 -> 10% nodes started.
(20m later)
meera (runtime): canary looks clean; no regressions. Will continue rollout to 50% then full if stable.
sasha (infra): confirming no paging alerts in us-east-1 or ap-southeast-1 — issue confined to eu-west-1 where the rollout happened.
chris (sre): customer impact summary for now: ~8-12% of hosted text-generation short requests in eu-west-1 experienced >2s tail, a handful of transient 502s tied to node paging. Dedicated clusters unaffected.
remy (prod-eng): putting incident broadcast into status page: "Performance degradation in eu-west-1 affecting a subset of short requests. Mitigation in progress." will update.
eli (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. Meera, taking ownership for next 6h?
meera (runtime): taking it. I'll keep rollout and dashboards in watch. ping me @ here any regressions.
eli (oncall): adding runbook checklist to thread: 1) verify fair_slotting enabled 2) confirm kv_cache trimmed under threshold 3) confirm patch rollout completion 4) customer comms updated 5) add postmortem owner.
meera (runtime): got it. created follow-up ticket: INC-2026-347 (postmortem). Owner: meera.
remy (prod-eng): postmortem scope: why grouping multiplier was changed without rollback guard, why automated smoke didn't catch long-tail impact, and add a pre-deploy test for mixed long/short workloads.
chris (sre): temporary followups: add metric alert for "kv_cache.per_conn_entries > 5000" and "batch_scheduler.slot_entropy < 0.6" to catch similar regressions earlier.
sasha (infra): saved snapshots of affected nodes for forensic: snapshot ids snap-eu-1451..snap-eu-1456.
ops-bot: 📌 Incident update logged. Incident state: Mitigated. Owner: meera (runtime). Next steps: full rollout of hotpatch, postmortem in 72h.
meera (runtime): final note before handoff: if fair_slotting or window toggles are reverted in future deploys, gate them behind 'mixed-workload-sim' smoke test in CI.
eli (oncall): thanks team. closing urgent loop. I'll join postmortem. :thumbsup:
(reacts: :white_check_mark: eli, :eyes: meera, :rocket: remy)
